content.content:
# Project, evaluation and classifier workflows

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/cli/release-workflows

Use the expanded CLI commands and understand their authorization and compute prerequisites.

These workflows target **neatlogs-cli@0.2.1**, pending npm publication, and retain the expanded operation set introduced in 0.2.0. Follow the [CLI quickstart](/cli) for host, profile, credential selection and project discovery. Check the package version before following a new command:

```bash
npm view neatlogs-cli dist-tags --json
neatlogs --version
```

Use a profile bound to your intended cloud region and project. OAuth login requests read scopes by default; request the write scopes for your chosen workflow explicitly. Current roles, entitlements and project membership apply to every request. Service-account support is declared separately on each [endpoint](/api-reference/endpoints).

## Keep the selected context for every command

Complete the quickstart in the same shell first: `NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST`,
`NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE` and `NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT` must identify the dashboard,
authenticated profile and project you selected. Define these helpers before
running the examples below:

```bash
nl_project() {
  neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" \
    --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" "$@"
}
nl_projects() {
  env -u NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" \
    --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile projects list "$@"
}
```

`nl_project` carries the chosen host, OAuth profile, credential source and
project through each read or mutation. `nl_projects` lists projects without an
explicit or environment-selected project, while retaining the same host and
OAuth identity. Both leave the application's SDK key available in the shell.

For 0.2.0, omit `--credential-source profile` from both definitions and prefix
each `neatlogs` invocation with `env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY -u NEATLOGS_TOKEN`.
Keep the existing `env -u NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` in `nl_projects` as well. Follow
these shell examples only for the operations you intend to perform; defining
the helpers does not execute a mutation.

## Project lifecycle and existing-member access

| Operation | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Archive / unarchive | Hides a project from normal active-project lists and restores it later. |
| Access grant / revoke | Adds or removes a project role override for an existing organization member. Removing an override preserves any access inherited from organization membership. |
| Soft delete | Uses the dashboard-equivalent project deletion behavior. It does not certify scheduled physical deletion or accepted-telemetry recovery. |

Project mutations require human OAuth with `project:write` and a role allowed to manage the project. Select the exact project before a lifecycle operation, and use the resource UUID required by `--confirm`:

```bash
nl_project projects current --json
nl_project projects archive --confirm '<project-uuid>' --idempotency-key '<unique-key>'
nl_projects --include-archived --json
nl_project projects unarchive --confirm '<project-uuid>' --idempotency-key '<new-key>'
```

Access updates do not invite new organization members:

```bash
nl_project projects access grant '<member-uuid>' --role project_viewer --idempotency-key '<unique-key>'
nl_project projects access revoke '<member-uuid>' --confirm '<member-uuid>' --idempotency-key '<new-key>'
```

See [project commands](/cli/commands/projects) for soft deletion and exact options. Lifecycle changes affect the selected project; use a disposable project when testing.

## Evaluation drafts and reviewer-aware activation

Saving an evaluation draft does not start review assignments. Before activating it, save its current form, choose eligible reviewers and define a review duration. Existing-trace evaluations also need a selected cohort.

```bash
nl_project evals get '<evaluation-uuid>' --json
nl_project evals form get '<evaluation-uuid>' --json
nl_project evals activate '<evaluation-uuid>' --body-stdin --idempotency-key '<unique-key>' <<'JSON'
{
  "reviewerUserIds": ["<reviewer-uuid>"],
  "reviewDuration": "1h",
  "maxItems": 100,
  "maxAssignments": 100
}
JSON
```

Activation requires human OAuth with `evaluation:write`. Reviewers must be eligible for the evaluation; duplicate or ineligible reviewer IDs are rejected. `maxItems` and `maxAssignments` bound the work admitted by this request. Reuse the same idempotency key only when retrying the exact request.

| Evaluation configuration | Activation behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Existing traces | Assigns the selected cohort using the saved current form. |
| Future one-time collection | Collects until its configured end, then applies the review window. |
| Recurring collection starting now | Can create a bounded first batch immediately. |
| Recurring collection starting later | Retains its future start and next-batch clock without a premature batch. |

**Scheduled collection caveat (October 6, 2026):** Production testing found that traces arriving after the last periodic matcher pass can be omitted from the final batch when collection ends. This affects short future windows and the last interval of longer windows. A backend fix is being prepared for Dev; until it is promoted and retested, independently verify the final cohort before relying on scheduled collection.

An active evaluation cannot be discarded as a draft. A never-launched draft can be discarded with its exact UUID:

```bash
nl_project evals discard '<evaluation-uuid>' --confirm '<evaluation-uuid>' --idempotency-key '<unique-key>'
```

Draft discard also removes its draft dependencies. It supports the credentials declared on its endpoint, including authorized service accounts. Review submission, evaluation completion and generated batch reports are separate outcomes; read their status independently. See [evaluation commands](/cli/commands/evals).

## Classifier labels, datasets, training and publication

The classifier workflow has explicit stages:

1. Create an unpublished classifier definition.
2. Save positive and negative labels referencing real spans in the selected project.
3. Request a bounded dataset job with an explicit budget.
4. Train against a ready dataset version with a separate explicit budget.
5. Publish a ready trained version for the selected span types.

```bash
nl_project classifiers create --body-stdin --idempotency-key '<unique-key>' <<'JSON'
{"displayName":"Support quality","method":"setfit"}
JSON
nl_project classifiers labels list '<classifier-uuid>' --limit 25 --json
nl_project classifiers datasets list '<classifier-uuid>' --limit 5 --json
nl_project classifiers training list '<classifier-uuid>' --limit 5 --json
```

Classifier reads use `configuration:read`; writes use `configuration:write` and human OAuth. Labels must reference spans belonging to the same project. A saved definition is not a trained model, and training does not automatically publish a detector.

Dataset and training requests require `budgetMicrousd`. One million micro-USD equals one US dollar. The request budget is an admission ceiling; it does not turn on a disabled deployment or bypass provider approval.

**The entire public classifier workflow is disabled in production as of October 6, 2026.** This includes creating definitions and reading definitions, labels, datasets, training and job status. The disabled `tier-c-compute` capability returns `404` / `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED` (CLI exit `5`). Provider-job admission is separately disabled. Detection suggestions, detection preview and analytics export share the disabled compute capability. Obtain workflow access and agreed limits before using these operations or starting provider jobs. Use [classifier commands](/cli/commands/classifiers) for exact bodies, job polling and cancellation.

| Problem | CLI result |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid label reference | Input/usage exit `2`. |
| Dataset or classifier not ready | Resource-state exit `6`. |
| Provider admission unavailable | Availability exit `7`; no provider job should be inferred from the request. |
| Response exceeds limits or fails its contract | Server/contract exit `11`. |

Read the structured problem's `code` and `requestId` when diagnosing a failure. Repeatedly retrying a disabled admission will not enable it.

## Bounded historical detection rescoring

Historical rescoring runs a detection over an explicitly limited range of existing traces. It is separate from Keyword Search indexing and project deletion.

Every request must supply all five limits:

| Field | Contract bound |
| --- | --- |
| `days` | 1–90 days |
| `maxTraces` | 1–1,000 traces |
| `batchSize` | 1–100 traces per batch |
| `maxDurationSeconds` | 60–3,600 seconds |
| `budgetMicrousd` | 1–100,000,000 micro-USD |

The job records progress so callers can poll its state and request cancellation. Admission, completion and cancellation are separate states; poll until a terminal result before treating the work as finished. The limits describe the request contract, not a recommended production backfill size.

Production execution requires separate compute admission and an explicitly approved historical-work plan. It remains gated in this release. See [detection commands](/cli/commands/detections) for `backfill`, `backfills get` and `backfills cancel`.

## Retry and readback

Use a fresh idempotency key for a new mutation and the original key for an exact retry. Wrong confirmation UUIDs are rejected before the intended mutation. Independently read the project, evaluation, classifier or job after changing it; a successful submission alone does not establish asynchronous completion.

The [operation availability guide](/api-reference/availability) distinguishes deployed contracts from enabled compute and accepted workflows. The [OpenAPI JSON](/openapi/public-api.json) provides the exact request and response schemas for client generation.

----
# Detections

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/features/detections

Automatically flag traces that match conditions, patterns, or classifiers.

Detections are rules that run against your traces and flag spans that match. They appear as annotations on top of your traces in the dashboard — so you can understand what happened in a run at a glance, without opening individual spans.

The key benefit: if you've created detections, you can scan your entire traces list and immediately see which runs had high token usage, which outputs contained PII, which agent decisions matched a pattern you care about — all without digging into the trace itself. Detections give you a summary layer on top of your data.

---

### How detections work

You define a detection rule — one of four types: regex, condition, PII detection, or classifier. Neatlogs evaluates it against spans as they come in. When a span matches, the detection appears as a badge on that trace in the traces list and inside the span detail panel.

A single trace can trigger multiple detections. Each one is labelled with the rule that triggered it, so you can filter the traces list by detection type.

<video src="/detections.mp4" autoPlay loop muted playsInline style={{ width: '100%', borderRadius: '8px' }} />

---

### Types of detections

#### Regex

Match against the text content of a span's input or output using a regular expression.

Use this when you're looking for a specific string pattern in what your agent produced — an action label, a structured output format, an error message, or a keyword that signals something worth reviewing.

**Examples:**
- Flag any trace where the agent output contains `TASK:` — useful if your agent assigns tasks and you want to track every run that produced one
- Detect when a tool response contains `"status": "failed"`
- Match a specific error string coming back from an API call

#### Condition

Flag spans based on numeric or boolean attributes — token counts, latency, cost, or any custom attribute you've set on a span.

Use this to surface operational signals: runs that were unusually expensive, slow, or that hit a threshold you care about.

**Examples:**
- `total_tokens > 8000` — flag runs where the model consumed significantly more tokens than usual
- `latency_ms > 5000` — catch responses that took longer than 5 seconds
- `tool_call_count > 10` — detect agents that looped more than expected
- `cost_usd > 0.10` — flag any single run that exceeded a cost threshold

#### PII detection

A built-in check that flags spans where the model input or output contains personally identifiable information: names, email addresses, phone numbers, financial data, and similar. No configuration needed — enable it and Neatlogs scans span content automatically.

Use this when your agent handles user-submitted text and you need visibility into whether PII is flowing through prompts or responses.

#### Classifier

Run a custom semantic check against span content. Classifiers go beyond exact pattern matching — they evaluate the meaning or category of the text rather than its literal value.

**Examples:**
- Flag traces where the agent output is off-topic or out of scope
- Detect when a retriever returned documents that don't match the query semantically
- Classify agent outputs by sentiment to surface negative user interactions
- Flag any span where the model response falls into a category you define

---

### What you see in the dashboard

Detections appear in two places:

1. **Traces list** — each trace shows its active detections as labelled badges. You can filter the entire list by detection type, so "show me all runs where high token usage was detected" is a single click.

2. **Span detail** — inside a trace, the specific span that triggered the detection is marked. You can see exactly which step caused the flag and what the matched content was.

<video src="/detections-on-traces.mp4" autoPlay loop muted playsInline style={{ width: '100%', borderRadius: '8px' }} />

<Callout type="info">
  Detections don't change how your agent runs. They are read-only annotations applied after spans are captured. Adding or removing a detection rule does not affect your application code.
</Callout>

---

### Example: meeting task agent

An agent that reads a meeting transcript and assigns tasks to team members might have:

- A **regex detection** matching `ASSIGNED TO:` to track every trace that produced a task assignment
- A **condition** on `total_tokens > 6000` to flag unusually long transcripts that drove up cost
- A **PII detection** to catch any run where participant names or email addresses leaked into the output
- A **classifier** to flag runs where the assigned tasks were off-topic or outside the agent's expected scope

Without opening a single trace, you can see: how many runs produced assignments today, which ones were expensive, whether any output contained PII, and whether the agent stayed on task — just from the traces list.

content.content:
# NeatLogs CLI

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/cli

Sign in through your browser and inspect your projects from a terminal.

An SDK project key in `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` sends traces and supports [SDK Doctor readback](/sdk/doctor); it does not authenticate public API CLI reads. If only that key is available, use Doctor and mark optional CLI readback **waiting on a human** until OAuth approval or a suitable service token is available.

Use the CLI to read traces, inspect detections, work with evaluations, and manage authorized project resources. People sign in with OAuth; CI and AI agents use [service-account tokens](/cli/automation).

## 1. Install

Use Node.js **22 or 24**. These instructions target the MIT-licensed **`neatlogs-cli@0.2.1`** release. Version 0.2.1 is pending npm publication; the install below will work after it is published. Check availability first:

```bash
npm view neatlogs-cli@0.2.1 version
npm install --global neatlogs-cli@0.2.1
neatlogs --version
```

The executable is `neatlogs`. You can verify the published package before installing it:

```bash
npm view neatlogs-cli dist-tags --json
```

The CLI includes the expanded 285-operation reference for project lifecycle, evaluation activation, classifier jobs and historical rescoring. Some workflows depend on enabled deployment capabilities. See [the workflows and their prerequisites](/cli/release-workflows).

## 2. Choose a profile and sign in

```bash
NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST='https://app.neatlogs.com'
NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE='neatlogs-us'
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" profile list
# Use this profile only if it is unused or already belongs to this host.
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth login
```

`--credential-source profile` selects stored OAuth credentials while keeping the application's SDK key available in the same shell. This option requires 0.2.1. On 0.2.0, omit it and prefix each OAuth command with `env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY -u NEATLOGS_TOKEN` in a POSIX shell. Other shells need the equivalent per-process environment exclusion.

In an interactive terminal, the CLI opens the browser for OAuth consent and prints a URL you can open manually. After you approve, return to the terminal; it stores the OAuth credentials in your operating-system vault.

In a headless terminal, the CLI selects Device Flow automatically. You can request it explicitly:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth login --device
```

Open the displayed verification URL on a device with a browser and approve the request. Never share the authorization URL, device code, or resulting credentials.

## 3. Select your project

List the projects your signed-in user can access. Discovery must receive neither `--project` nor `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID`; the POSIX command below excludes the variable only for that process:

```bash
env -u NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile projects list
```

Set the chosen project UUID for the read commands:

```bash
NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT='<project-uuid>'

neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" whoami
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" projects current
```

Profiles store non-secret host and context preferences. OAuth credentials are stored separately and bound to the host and profile.

For EU, set `NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST` to `https://eu.app.neatlogs.com` and use a separate profile such as `neatlogs-eu`. Keep the same host and profile for login and every read; do not rebind an authenticated profile from another dashboard.
The same package serves both regions once the corresponding public API is
deployed. See [US and EU profiles](/cli/configuration#us-and-eu-profiles).

## 4. Read project data

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" traces list --limit 5
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" detections list --limit 5
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" evals list --limit 5
```

For a known trace:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" traces get '<trace-id>' --json
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" traces spans list '<trace-id>' --limit 25 --json
```

`--json` provides structured output for scripts. Cursor-list commands can collect several pages with an explicit ceiling:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile --project "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROJECT" traces list --all --max-items 500 --json
```

For bounded analytics, pagination, and collaboration prerequisites, see [tested CLI workflows](/cli/workflows).

## Permissions and troubleshooting

Version `0.2.1` retains read-oriented default scopes, including detection reads through `configuration:read`. Earlier `0.1.0-team-test.6` requested the complete CLI scope set. Current roles and entitlements still apply. Use `--scope` to request the permissions for a particular workflow:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth login \
  --scope context:read observability:read evaluation:read configuration:read offline_access
```

For a workflow that also writes evaluations, request its required scopes explicitly:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth login \
  --scope context:read observability:read evaluation:read evaluation:write offline_access
```

For service-account setup or managed credential creation and revocation, sign in with the access scopes those operations require. The default login does not include `access:write`:

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth login \
  --scope context:read organization:read access:read access:write offline_access
```

These administration commands require a human OAuth identity and current permission to manage the target service account or project credential. Token scopes granted to the automation identity are separate from the OAuth scopes used to administer it.

In 0.2.1, `auth status` verifies the credential with the public API and requires `context:read`; it needs no project selection. A successful status does not prove permission to read a particular project or trace. In 0.2.0, status can report `authenticated: true` for an SDK key that the public API rejects: use project-scoped `whoami` and an actual trace read as the authoritative checks. See [authentication recovery](/cli/configuration#authentication-verification-and-recovery).

Your current role must also allow the operation. A `403` means a scope, role, binding, or entitlement is missing; [API error guidance](/api-reference/errors) explains other failures.

Upgrading the CLI does not change scopes already issued to stored OAuth credentials. After upgrading to the stable release, log out of the selected profile and sign in again to apply its new default scopes. Request write scopes explicitly for workflows that need them.

On Linux, OAuth credential storage requires libsecret and a running Secret Service. The CLI reports an error when the vault is unavailable. [Credential storage options](/cli/configuration) explain the explicit file-storage fallback for supported POSIX systems.

```bash
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth status
neatlogs --help
neatlogs traces --help
neatlogs --host "$NEATLOGS_CLI_HOST" --profile "$NEATLOGS_CLI_PROFILE" --credential-source profile auth logout
```

# MCP Server

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/integrations/mcp

Let your coding agent query Neatlogs traces, detections, and fix suggestions.

Neatlogs exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so your coding agent can read your observability data directly — search traces, pull the full context of a failing run, check detections, and act on fix suggestions — without you copying anything out of the dashboard.

---

### Connect

The easiest way is the [wizard](/docs/quickstart/wizard), which offers to wire the MCP server into Claude Code or Cursor at the end of its run, or on its own:

```bash
npx @neatlogs/wizard mcp --api-key YOUR_PROJECT_KEY
```

To connect manually, add a `neatlogs` entry to your client's MCP config. The server speaks Streamable HTTP and authenticates with your project API key as a bearer token:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "neatlogs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_PROJECT_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The config file depends on your client — for example `.mcp.json` for Claude Code or `.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor. The MCP server lives at `/mcp` on the **same host as your SDK endpoint** (the hosted default is `https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`; use your own host's `/mcp` if you self-host). Running `npx @neatlogs/wizard` wires this up for you.

<Callout type="info">
  The wizard merges this entry into your existing config without clobbering other MCP servers you've already set up.
</Callout>

---

### What your agent can do

Once connected, the agent has tools to read and act on your Neatlogs data:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search_traces` | Search traces by free-text query (BM25 keyword by default, or semantic vector search) |
| `get_trace_context` | Pull a trace's full context — metrics, span tree with inputs/outputs and code locations, and the detections that fired |
| `list_detections` | List the active detections enabled on the project |
| `get_detection_trend` | Get hourly / daily / weekly occurrence counts for a single detection |
| `triage_list` | List the current fix suggestions |
| `triage_get` | Get the full detail of one fix — root cause and recommended action |
| `triage_get_investigation` | Read the investigation that produced a fix — the root-cause reasoning trail |
| `triage_list_steps` | List the steps of an investigation thread |
| `triage_accept` / `triage_dismiss` / `triage_update_status` / `triage_update` | Act on a fix — accept, dismiss, move across the board, or update it |
| `log_trace` | Push a trace from your coding agent into Neatlogs |
| `ping` / `whoami` | Health check and identify the project this MCP session is bound to |

This turns a debugging loop into a conversation: ask your agent *"what's failing in production?"*, have it search traces and inspect the worst one, then let it read the matching fix suggestion and apply it — all in the editor.

---

### Related

- [Traces](/docs/features/traces) — the same data, viewed in the dashboard
- [Detections](/docs/features/detections) — the rules `list_detections` reports on
- [Fixes](/docs/features/triage) — the suggestions these tools read and update

# Fixes

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/features/triage

AI-generated fix suggestions from failing traces — reviewed, then dispatched to a coding agent.

Detections tell you *what* went wrong. **Fixes** proposes *how* — Neatlogs analyzes failing and flagged traces, produces a concrete fix suggestion with root-cause reasoning, and lets you push it to a coding agent that opens a pull request, without leaving the dashboard.

<video src="/fixes.mp4" autoPlay loop muted playsInline style={{ width: '100%', borderRadius: '8px' }} />

---

### Suggestions

A **suggestion** is an AI-generated proposal to fix an issue found in a trace. Each one includes:

- **Title and description** — what the problem is, in plain language
- **Analysis** — the root-cause reasoning behind the issue
- **Location** — where in your code the issue likely originates
- **Code improvements and best practices** — concrete changes to make
- **References** — links to relevant docs or context

Suggestions live on the **Fixes** board, split into **Active**, **Resolved**, and **Drafts** tabs. Search and filter them — by severity, source, category, traces, or staleness — and open any one to see its full detail and the investigation that produced it.

![The Fixes board — active, resolved, and draft suggestions with severity score, workflow, source, and category](/triage-board.png)

---

### The investigation trail

Behind every suggestion is an **investigation**: the step-by-step reasoning trail the orchestrator followed while building the fix — each tool call and LLM hop it made to localize the bug and decide on a change. The investigation panel shows this trail and the linked traces, so you can see *why* a fix was proposed, not just what it is. (Your coding agent can re-hydrate this same context through the [MCP server](/integrations/mcp) when resuming a fix in a fresh session.)

---

### Dispatching a fix to a coding agent

When a suggestion looks right, push it to a coding agent. Neatlogs dispatches the fix — with the suggestion's prompt, your linked GitHub repo, branch, and chosen model — to the agent, then polls until it finishes. When the agent opens a pull request, the PR link is hydrated back onto the suggestion, and you can mark it deployed once shipped.

<Callout type="info">
  Cursor Cloud Agents are supported today, with Claude Code and Codex workers planned. Dispatching requires a connected GitHub repository — see [Integrations](/docs/features/integrations).
</Callout>

<video src="/triage.mp4" autoPlay loop muted playsInline style={{ width: '100%', borderRadius: '8px' }} />

---

### How Fixes relates to the rest of Neatlogs

- It builds on [Detections](/docs/features/detections) and trace failures — those are the signals that surface issues worth fixing.
- The [MCP server](/integrations/mcp) exposes your fixes and their investigations to your coding agent, so you can review and apply a fix from your editor (`triage_list`, `triage_get`, `triage_get_investigation`, `triage_accept`, `triage_update_status`).
- Suggestions support [comments](/docs/features/comments), so your team can discuss a proposed fix before dispatching it.

# Prompt Templates and Managed Prompts

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/sdk/prompt-templates

Track prompt templates in telemetry and use the separate authenticated managed-prompt API.

Prompt templates let you capture both the template structure and the runtime variable values for every LLM call, linking them to the span in the dashboard. This makes it possible to see exactly what was sent to the model for any trace, and compare how different variable values affect outputs.

### `SystemPromptTemplate` and `UserPromptTemplate`

`SystemPromptTemplate` is for the system/instruction prompt. `UserPromptTemplate` is for the user/human turn. Both accept either a plain string or a list of message dicts, with `{{variable}}` placeholders.

```python
from neatlogs import SystemPromptTemplate, UserPromptTemplate

system_template = SystemPromptTemplate([
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a {{role}} assistant. Context: {{context}}"},
])

user_template = UserPromptTemplate([
    {"role": "user", "content": "{{question}}"},
])
```

> `PromptTemplate` (and the `prompt_template=` keyword on `trace()`) are kept as backward-compatible aliases for `SystemPromptTemplate` / `system_prompt_template=`. Both work; new code should use the canonical names.

Call `.compile(**variables)` to fill in the placeholders and get the rendered messages:

```python
system_messages = system_template.compile(role="support", context=context_text)
# Returns: [{"role": "system", "content": "You are a support assistant. Context: ..."}]
```

`.compile()` also stores the template and variable values in context so Neatlogs can link them to the next LLM span.

### Using Templates with `trace(kind="LLM")`

Wrap the `.compile()` call and the LLM invocation inside `with neatlogs.trace(kind="LLM", system_prompt_template=...)`. Place this at the **smallest unit** containing the actual LLM call:

```python
from neatlogs import SystemPromptTemplate, UserPromptTemplate
from openai import OpenAI

system_template = SystemPromptTemplate([
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a {{role}} assistant. Context: {{context}}"},
])
user_template = UserPromptTemplate([
    {"role": "user", "content": "{{question}}"},
])

@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
def answer_agent(question: str, context: str) -> str:
    with neatlogs.trace("answer_prompt", kind="LLM",
                        system_prompt_template=system_template,
                        user_prompt_template=user_template):
        system_messages = system_template.compile(role="support", context=context)
        user_messages = user_template.compile(question=question)

        response = OpenAI().chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o",
            messages=system_messages + user_messages,
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content
```

---

## Managed Prompts


Unpinned prompt reads use a 60-second in-process cache by default. A fresh entry returns immediately. After expiry, the current SDKs use stale-while-revalidate: the caller receives the last usable value while one background refresh updates the cache. A refresh failure preserves that stale value and a later lookup retries. Request a specific `version` when a deployment must remain pinned.

> **Note:** `neatlogs.init()` must be called before module-level prompt methods (`get_prompt`, `create_prompt`, etc.). An explicitly constructed `PromptClient` or `AsyncPromptClient` uses its own API key and endpoint and does not require `init()`.

## Managed-prompt privacy, ownership, and retention

| Concern | Contract |
|---|---|
| Data path | Prompt content, messages, variables, labels, tags, and configuration are sent intentionally to the managed-prompt API. This is not OTLP telemetry. |
| Authentication | The SDK sends the project API key configured by `init()` as bearer/API-key authentication. Keep the key in a secret manager or environment variable, never in source. |
| Endpoint | The client uses the SDK base endpoint; hosted Neatlogs defaults to `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`. A custom/self-hosted endpoint applies to both telemetry and managed-prompt calls. |
| Ownership | A project API key is bound to one project. Prompt names and versions are resolved inside that project; a caller cannot select another project while using that key. Dashboard sessions are separately checked for project membership. |
| Retention | Versions are stored as project data. Deleting a managed-prompt version removes it from active reads by soft deletion; the API does not promise immediate physical erasure or a fixed purge interval. Organization/account deletion cascades project prompt data. Use your account's retention agreement for deletion-time guarantees. |

<Callout type="warn">
  Telemetry `mask=` callbacks do not run on managed-prompt HTTP requests. Enabling local masking or server-side telemetry PII redaction does not mean prompt CRUD content was transformed. If content must be redacted before prompt storage, transform it explicitly before calling the prompt API. There is no prompt-transform option today.
</Callout>

```python

neatlogs.init(
    api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"],
)

prompt = neatlogs.get_prompt("support-system-prompt")
```


await init({ apiKey: process.env.NEATLOGS_API_KEY });
const prompt = await getPrompt('support-system-prompt');
```

### Get and use a prompt

Fetch the prompt, wrap in a `SystemPromptTemplate` for tracking, and pass it to `with neatlogs.trace(kind="LLM", system_prompt_template=...)`:

```python
from neatlogs import SystemPromptTemplate

@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
def answer_agent(question: str, context: str) -> str:
    # Default: most recently created version
    prompt = neatlogs.get_prompt("support-system-prompt")
    prompt_template = SystemPromptTemplate(prompt.content)

    with neatlogs.trace("answer_prompt", kind="LLM", system_prompt_template=prompt_template):
        messages = prompt.compile_messages({"context": context, "question": question})
        response = openai_client.chat.completions.create(
            model="gpt-4o",
            messages=messages,
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content
```

By a specific label:

```python
prompt = neatlogs.get_prompt("support-system-prompt", label="staging")
```

By a specific version:

```python
prompt = neatlogs.get_prompt("support-system-prompt", version=3)
```


const staging = await getPrompt('support-system-prompt', { label: 'staging' });
const v3 = await getPrompt('support-system-prompt', { version: 3 });
```

### List

```python
# All prompts
prompts = neatlogs.list_prompts()

# Filter by name or label
prompts = neatlogs.list_prompts(name="support-system-prompt", label="production")
```

### Create

```python
# Text prompt
neatlogs.create_prompt(
    name="greeting-prompt",
    prompt="Hello {{name}}, how can I help you?",
    labels=["production"],
)

# Chat prompt
neatlogs.create_prompt(
    name="support-system-prompt",
    prompt=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a {{role}} assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "{{question}}"},
    ],
    type="chat",
    labels=["production"],
)
```

### Promote a version (update labels)

Move a label to a specific version, for example to promote `v3` to production:

```python
neatlogs.update_prompt(
    name="support-system-prompt",
    version=3,
    new_labels=["production"],
)
```

### Save as new version

```python
neatlogs.save_as_version(
    prompt_name="support-system-prompt",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert {{role}} assistant."},
    ],
    labels=["staging"],
    commit_message="More assertive tone",
)
```

### Delete a prompt version

Soft-deletes a specific version by name and version number:

```python
neatlogs.delete_prompt("support-system-prompt", version=1)
```

### Remove a tag

Remove a tag from a specific prompt version:

```python
neatlogs.remove_tag("support-system-prompt", version=3, tag="candidate")
```

### Async fetching

In an async application, use `neatlogs.aget_prompt(...)` — the coroutine version of `get_prompt`, with the same arguments — so you don't block the event loop on the fetch:

```python

prompt = await neatlogs.aget_prompt("support-system-prompt", label="production")
```

For repeated fetches you can hold an `AsyncPromptClient` directly (call `await client.close()` when done). Direct clients use the credentials passed to their constructor. The module-level `neatlogs.fetch_prompt(name, label=...)` returns a raw `CachedPrompt` and requires `init()` first.


The module-level functions share the `PromptClient` created by `init()`. Construct a client directly when you need an explicit cache lifetime or a separate project:

# FAQ

URL: https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/faq

Frequently asked questions and common troubleshooting tips.

### My traces are not showing up in the dashboard

The most common cause is that `neatlogs.init()` silently disabled export because it couldn't find your API key.

### How it happens

When `neatlogs.init()` runs without a valid API key, it automatically disables data export internally. Your code still runs normally (spans are created, decorators work, logs are captured) but nothing is sent to the backend. There is no error by default, so it's easy to miss.

```python
# This silently disables export (no key provided, no env var set)
neatlogs.init()
```

### How to fix it

**Option 1: Set the environment variable (recommended)**

```bash
export NEATLOGS_API_KEY="your-project-api-key"
```

Then call `init()` without the `api_key` argument. It picks up the env var automatically:

```python
neatlogs.init()
```

This is the recommended approach because it keeps secrets out of your code and works consistently across local development, CI, and production environments.

**Option 2: Use a `.env` file** (with `python-dotenv` or similar)

```bash
# .env
REDACTED
```

```python
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv()

neatlogs.init()
```

**Option 3: Pass the key directly**

```python
neatlogs.init(api_key="your-project-api-key")
```

Avoid hardcoding the key in source code. Use this only for quick local testing.

### How to confirm export is working

Enable debug mode to see what's happening:

content.content:
**Product features**
- **Traces & Detections:** Monitors every production run, surfaces failures, and groups related cases into incidents.
- **Investigations:** Provides evidence, root cause, and a fix brief that coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex can use.
- **Evals:** Scores runs against a shared rubric, with an AI evaluator and human reviewers.
- **Collaboration:** Connects support, product, and engineering through Slack, Linear, and Notion, with "Ask @neatlogs" for plain-English questions.
- **Context attachment:** Adds customer feedback and business context to agent runs.
- **Dashboards:** Builds custom dashboards from plain-language requests.
- **Trace import:** Imports from LangSmith, Braintrust, Langfuse, Phoenix, and OpenTelemetry.
- **Fix verification:** Checks that fixes hold in production.

**Plans and limits** (prices in USD)

| Plan | Price | Spans/month | Investigations | AI evals | Users / projects | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 100k (hard cap) | 3 | Human evals unlimited | 2 users, 1 project | 14 days |
| Starter | $99 ($84 annual) | 250k, then $10 per 100k | 50, then $25 per 10 | 5,000, then $15 per 2,500 | Unlimited users, 5 projects | 30 days |
| Pro | $499 ($424 annual) | 1M, then $8 per 100k | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited users, projects | 90 days |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom |

- Detectors: 5 on Free, 10 trained classifiers on Starter, 100 on Pro, and unlimited detectors on Pro.
- Starter adds PII redaction, roles, and webhooks. Pro adds audit log and SSO.
- Enterprise adds SAML/SCIM, data residency, VPC or self-hosted ingest, and an SLA.
- Paid plans include unlimited users. Bring-your-own model key has no extra cost.

**APIs, CLI, MCP, evals, and datasets**
- **APIs/SDKs:** Python, TypeScript, OpenTelemetry, a REST API (HTTP injection), and an open SDK.
- **CLI:** `neatlogs ask` runs investigations from the terminal.
- **MCP:** Integration available for Cursor and Copilot.
- **Evals:** Rubric-based scoring with AI and human evaluators, subject to the plan limits above.
- **Datasets:** Not mentioned on the page.

Usage: `neatlogs evals schedules update [options] <schedule-id>`

### Arguments

| Argument | Requirement | Description | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `--batch-schedule <duration>` | Required option | recurrence duration from 1h to 8760h, 1d to 365d, or 1w to 52w | — |
| `--idempotency-key <key>` | Optional option | stable UUID for retrying the same logical schedule update | — |

content.text:
I mapped the neatlogs features a Python CLI like FirstRun can use. Three things I expected to work cannot be set up from code:

- **Feedback:** the Python SDK has no feedback or score function. The trace feedback API accepts only a human sign-in, not a service-account token.
- **AI evaluator on a question:** you can only attach an AI evaluator to an evaluation question in the dashboard. The API schema for the evaluation form has no field for it.
- **On-demand evaluator runs:** these are disabled in production. This matches the `NOT_FOUND_OR_OPERATION_DISABLED` error already recorded in `evidence/neatlogs.md`.

Source: the full docs bundle at `https://docs.neatlogs.com/llms-full.txt` (459 pages) and the OpenAPI spec at `https://docs.neatlogs.com/openapi/public-api.json` (285 operations). I wrote no files in the repo and called no write API. Read-only checks: the installed SDK is 1.4.26, and the npm `latest` tag for `neatlogs-cli` is 0.2.1, although the docs still call 0.2.1 "pending publication".

## Credentials

There are three kinds:

- **SDK project key** (`NEATLOGS_API_KEY`): sends traces, works with the SDK prompt functions, and authenticates the MCP server. It cannot read through the Public API.
- **Service-account token**: for CI and scripts. Create it in **Settings → Service Accounts**.
- **Human OAuth**: `neatlogs auth login`. Some write operations accept only this.

Every Public API request uses the same base and headers:
```http
https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public/...
Authorization: Bearer <service-account-token or OAuth token>
x-project-id: <project-uuid>
idempotency-key: <uuid4>   # required on every mutation; rejected on reads
```

- **Scopes:** `observability:read/write`, `evaluation:read/write`, `configuration:read/write`, `context:read`.
- **Response shape:** success is `{success, requestId, data}`. Errors use `application/problem+json`.
- **Pagination:** cursors expire after 15 minutes. Trace lists take a `limit` of 1 to 50.

## Features

"SA" means a service-account token works. "OAuth only" means it needs a human CLI login.

| Feature | How to set it up | Exact call | Limits and gates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions | SDK | `@neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW", session_id=...)`, `neatlogs.trace(name, session_id=...)`, or `with neatlogs.identify(session_id=, parent_session_id=, session_custom_fields={...})` | If you omit it, `session_id` equals `trace_id`. `identify()` does not carry across processes. |
| End user and metadata | SDK | `trace(..., end_user_id=str(uid), end_user_metadata={"plan":"pro"})` or the same arguments on `identify()` | Set it on the root span only. It is not an `init()` argument. Filter with `metadata:plan`. |
| Operator ID and tags | SDK | `init(user_id=..., tags=[...])`. Extra `wrap()` kwargs become `neatlogs.workflow.<key>`. | Tags apply to the whole process. |
| Change trace tags or name later | API (SA) | `PATCH /traces/{traceId}` with `{"expectedRevision":int,"tags":[...≤10],"traceName":"..."}` | Needs the `public-api-mutations` capability. |
| Trace feedback (rating) | **API, OAuth only** | `POST /traces/{traceId}/feedback` with `{"rating":-100..100,"accuracy":"≤50 chars","comment":"...","expectedResponse":"...","issueTypes":[≤20]}` | No SDK function exists. SA tokens are not accepted. |
| Span thumbs up or down | API, OAuth only | `PUT /traces/{t}/spans/{s}/feedback` with `{"vote":"up"\|"down","note":"..."}` | Also in the dashboard ("Voting"). |
| Bulk feedback | API, OAuth only | `POST /feedback/bulk` with `{"items":[{"action":"trace_feedback.create","itemKey":"k1","target":{"traceId":"..."},"body":{...}}]}` | 1 to 100 items. Also `span_feedback.set` and related actions. |
| AI evaluator definition | API (SA) or CLI `evaluators create --body-stdin` | `POST /evaluators` with `{"name","type":"llm_judge"\|"agent_judge","systemPrompt"≤20000,"modelProvider","modelName","maxBudgetUsd"≤100,"maxToolCalls"1-50 (default 12),"reasoningEnabled","outputSpec":[{"key","label","scoreType":"boolean\|numeric\|categorical\|text","options","required"}],"toolGrants":[{"provider":"neatlogs_mcp\|composio\|http_get\|custom_mcp","toolName","config"}]}` | — |
| Run an evaluator on one trace | OAuth only | `POST /evaluators/{id}/runs` with `{"traceId","spanId"}` and `/playground` | Gated by `tier-c-compute`, which is disabled in production. |
| Evaluation (scheduled or online) | API (SA) or CLI `evals create` | `POST /evaluations` with `{"name","type":"human"\|"ai","traceSource":"existing"\|"future","sendFrequency":"immediate\|batched\|manual","batchSchedule":"24h\|1d\|1w","samplingRate":1-100,"dailyLimit","startsAt","endsAt","traceFilter":{workflowName,tags,status,span_names,span_types,detectionNames,sessionIds,endUserIds,cost_min/max,latency_min_ms/max_ms,...}}` | Known bug: a future collection can miss traces that arrive after the last matcher pass. |
| Evaluation form | API (SA) | `PUT /evaluations/{id}/form` with `{"name","questions":[{"answerType":"rating\|linear_scale\|multiple_choice\|...","questionText","sortOrder","options"}]}` | **The schema has no field to assign an AI evaluator to a question.** The docs show this only in the dashboard. |
| Activate, launch, dispatch | Activate and launch are OAuth only. Dispatch works with SA. | `POST .../activate` with `{"reviewerUserIds":[...],"reviewDuration":"1h","maxItems","maxAssignments"}`. `POST .../batches/dispatch` with `{"maxItems"≤1000,"maxAssignments"≤10000}`. | — |
| Read eval results | API (SA) | `GET /evaluations/{id}/responses`, `.../progress`, `.../batches/{b}/report`, `/traces/{t}/evaluations`, `/evaluations-stats` | CSV and JSON export are available. |
| Datasets | Not available | — | The Experiments page says "Coming soon". Only classifier datasets exist, and those are disabled. |
| Prompt management | SDK (project key) or API (SA) | `neatlogs.get_prompt(name, label="production" \| version=3)`, `aget_prompt`, `list_prompts`, `create_prompt(name, prompt=..., type="chat", labels=[...])`, `update_prompt(name, version, new_labels=[...])`, `save_as_version(prompt_name, messages, labels, commit_message)`, `delete_prompt`, `remove_tag`. API: `POST /prompts` and `PUT /prompts/{id}/label`. | Reads use a 60 s cache with stale-while-revalidate. `mask=` does not apply to prompt calls. |
| Prompt playground | Dashboard only | — | Needs your own provider keys in Settings → AI Providers. |
| Alerts | API (SA) or CLI `alerts create` | `POST /alert-rules` with `{"name","ruleType":"threshold\|per_event\|compound\|ingestion_health\|metric_threshold","severity","detectionId","thresholdCount","windowMinutes","cooldownMinutes","conditions":[{"detection","operator","threshold"}],"metricName":"cost\|latency\|error_rate\|tokens_total\|trace_count\|tool_failure_rate\|detection_rate...","metricAggregation":"sum\|avg\|p95\|p99\|count\|rate...","metricOperator","metricThresholdValue","silenceMinutes","channelMask":{"email","slack","webhookIds":[≤1]}}`. Test: `POST /alert-rules/{id}/test`. | — |
| Webhooks | API (SA) | `POST /webhooks` with `{"name","destinationUrl","eventTypes":["alert.threshold_breach","notify.eval_completed",...],"secret"}` | Fire history: `GET /alert-history`. |
| Detections | API (SA) or CLI | `POST /detections` with `{"displayName","groupId","type":"regex"\|"conditional"\|"pii"\|"classifier","config":{...},"runOn":{"frequency":"trace\|span_type\|span_name","span_names":[...]},"threshold"}`. Reads: `/detections/{id}/hits` and `/trends`. | `generate`, `preview`, suggestions and backfill are OAuth only and `tier-c-compute`, so disabled. Built-in classifiers are only `jailbreaking`, `nsfw`, `hate` and `refusals`. |
| Investigate | **Dashboard only** | — | No Public API endpoint exists. The MCP server reads only the investigations attached to Fixes. The neatlogs.com homepage advertises `neatlogs ask`, but the docs command reference does not list it. |
| Fixes | Dashboard, or the MCP tools `triage_*` | — | Dispatch needs a connected GitHub repository. Only Cursor Cloud Agents are supported today. |
| Query traces, cost and analytics | API (SA, or the legacy key) or CLI | `GET /traces?from&to&status&workflowName&sessionId&limit&cursor`, `GET /traces/{id}/spans`, `GET /traces/{id}/export`, `POST /analytics/cost` with `{"from","to","filters":{"workflowNames","statuses":["OK","ERROR"],"sessionIds","detections"}}`. Also `/analytics/kpis`, `errors`, `tools`, `waste`, `time`, `chart`, and `POST /search/traces/semantic` with `{"q","workflowName","limit"≤50}`. | `/analytics/export` is disabled (`tier-c-compute`). |
| MCP server | Project SDK key | URL `https://ingest.neatlogs.com/mcp`, header `Authorization: Bearer <project key>`. Tools: `search_traces`, `get_trace_context`, `list_detections`, `get_detection_trend`, `triage_*`, `log_trace`, `whoami`. | — |
| SDK self-check | SDK | `python -m neatlogs doctor --local --json`, then `--probe --json` | The probe reads its own test trace back. |

## CLI (`neatlogs-cli`)

Install with `npm i -g neatlogs-cli@0.2.1`. It needs Node 22 or 24. The binary is `neatlogs`.

Command groups: account, alerts, analytics, api, api-keys, auth, billing, classifiers, coding-tools, comments, completion, credential-migrations, credentials, detections, evals, evaluators, feedback, filters, groups, guest, guest-links, imports, incidents, ingest-credentials, integrations, mcp, notifications, orgs, profile, projects, prompts, schema, service-accounts, sessions, sharing, skills, traces, usage, version, webhooks, whoami.

Useful subcommands:
- **feedback:** `feedback create --trace <id> --body-stdin`, plus `span-set` and `bulk`.
- **evals:** `evals create`, `form set`, `activate`, `batches dispatch`, `schedules update --batch-schedule 1d`, `responses`, `stats --period 7d`.
- **traces:** `traces list --all --max-items 500 --json`, `traces semantic-search`, `traces update-metadata`.
- **analytics:** `analytics cost` and related commands.
- **any operation:** `neatlogs api <operationId> --param --query --body-stdin`.

For CI, run `neatlogs --host https://app.neatlogs.com --credential-source token --project <uuid> ...` with `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` set.

## Plan Limits From the neatlogs.com Pricing Page

The hackathon lifted these, but here they are:
- **Pro:** 1M spans per month, unlimited Investigations and AI evals, 90-day retention.
- **Starter:** 5,000 AI evals, 50 Investigations, 30-day retention.

Separately, service-account administration and token minting share one rate-limit bucket. It holds 10 requests and refills at 10 per hour.

## Where the Docs Say Nothing

The docs do not cover:
- a span-level "score" attribute that feeds evals;
- how `type:"ai"` on an evaluation chooses an evaluator;
- a dataset or experiment API;
- an Investigate API.

## Pages Read

Everything below is under `https://docs.neatlogs.com`:
- **SDK:** `/sdk/python`, `/sdk/sessions`, `/sdk/end-user-identity`, `/sdk/tags`, `/sdk/custom-attributes`, `/sdk/prompt-templates`, `/sdk/span-kinds`, `/sdk/http-injection`
- **Features:** `/docs/features/evals`, `/evals/ai-evaluators`, `/evals/human-evaluators`, `/experiments`, `/alerts`, `/detections`, `/ai-search`, `/triage`, `/traces`, plus `/docs/faq`
- **API:** `/api-reference`, `/quickstart`, `/authentication`, `/availability`, `/errors`, `/pagination`, `/idempotency`, and the endpoint pages for traces, feedback, evaluators, evaluations, alert-rules, detections, analytics, search, prompts and webhooks
- **CLI and MCP:** `/cli`, `/cli/commands` and its subpages, `/cli/release-workflows`, `/integrations/mcp`

Outside the docs I read `https://neatlogs.com` and `https://pypi.org/project/neatlogs/`. Local copies of the split pages are in the session scratchpad, under `nl/pages/`.
